text: set_glyph ( * , glyph_name : str , glyph_data : dict [ str , Any ], create : bool | None = None , dry_run : bool | None = None , font_id : int | None = None , font_name : str | None = None ) -> Any Whole-glyph replacement or creation. Prefer a scoped editing tool when it supports the requested change and preserves unrelated data. Replace a whole glyph with writable VFJ JSON, or create with create:true. Supports layers, outlines/nodes, components and element transforms, anchors, hints/guidelines, groups, paint and metadata; discover exact structure with get_vfj_schema. When replacing an existing glyph, read full get_glyph and preserve unrelated data. Construction summaries are not VFJ. nodes_list takes precedence over nodes. dry_run validates a detached glyph without committing. Pass glyph_data as an object. Omitted fields use native defaults; this is NOT a patch. See schema overview for replacement and serialization limitations. Parameters: glyph_name (str, required): Glyph name to replace or create. create (bool, optional): Create the glyph if missing; default false. dry_run (bool, optional): Validate and summarize without modifying the font or undo history; default false. glyph_data (dict[str, Any], required): Full VFJ glyph object: name, unicode/unicodes, layers and metadata. Get detailed nested definitions with get_vfj_schema(topic=glyph). font_id (float, optional): Optional FontLab package id. font_name (str, optional): Optional font name match. Effect: replace/create glyph with Undo. Returns: {status:"validated",would_create,glyph_name,catalog_version,layers,validation,warnings} for dry_run; {status:"ok",created,glyph:glyph_summary} after commit Notes: This example makes a simple rectangular outline named H, not a designed H letter. create defaults false. create:true updates an existing glyph too; it is not create-only. Supply a VFJ glyph object, never an entire font document. Replaces all layers and copies mark, note, lib, tags, selections, Unicode encodings, OpenType class/variation-selector data and Sigma metadata. Omitted writable values reset; use the complete readback as the edit base. glyph_name selects and names the target; do not rely on glyph_data.name to rename it. Unicode is VFJ hex text, e.g. "0048". Use get_glyph output to preserve fields during edits. Request the relevant get_vfj_schema topic directly when its definition is needed; overview is optional discovery. dry_run:true performs the same structural and detached native parsing as a write, without committing or adding undo history. Errors identify JSON paths where available. Native normalization ranges are checked for affine offsets and layer widths. A parsed glyph does not prove component dependency validity, expression results, or rendering correctness; verify readback. Embedded chat allows glyph_data up to 262144 UTF-16 code units (compact JSON). Glyph/schema reads are kept intact up to 524288 code units; larger reads fail explicitly. These are chat-specific limits, not VFJ format limits. Catalog validation intentionally supports its own documented JSON Schema vocabulary; it is not a general-purpose validator. Legacy opaque metadata remains extensible. # Example result = fontpr . set_glyph ( font_id = 101 , glyph_name = 'H' , create = True , glyph_data = { 'name' : 'H' , 'unicode' : '0048' , 'layers' : [{ 'name' : 'Regular' , 'advanceWidth' : 640 , 'elements' : [{ 'elementData' : { 'contours' : [{ 'nodes' : [ '80 0' , '180 0' , '180 700' , '80 700' ]}]}}]}]}) Source: FontLab MCP specification
title: fontpr.set_glyph

text: set_glyph_anchors ( * , glyph_name : str , anchors : list [ dict [ str , Any ]], font_id : int | None = None , font_name : str | None = None , layer_name : str | None = None ) -> Any Patch named anchors on one existing non-Auto layer. Each patch has name and optional x,y,expression_x,expression_y,cloud_enabled,mark_enabled or remove=true. New anchors require x and y. Coordinates clear expressions on that axis unless an expression is supplied. All patches are validated before application; unrelated anchors and other layers are preserved. mark_enabled requires cloud_enabled. Auto Layer anchors must be edited at their source. Undo supported. Parameters: font_id (float, optional): Optional package id. font_name (str, optional): Optional font name. glyph_name (str, required): Exact glyph name. layer_name (str, optional): Exact layer; defaults to active layer. anchors (list[dict[str, Any]], required) Effect: glyph mutation with Undo. Returns: {status:"ok",glyph_name,construction} Notes: Existing non-Auto layer only. All 1–64 patches validate before changes. New anchors need numeric x and y; existing anchors can be partially patched. Unique nonempty names <=128 characters. Coordinates finite and absolute value <=10000000. expression_x/y strings <=256 characters. Numeric coordinate clears its expression unless an expression is supplied in the same patch. remove:true permits only name and remove and requires an existing anchor. Unknown fields error. mark_enabled:true requires cloud_enabled. Patch source anchors instead of generated Auto Layer anchors. # Example result = fontpr . set_glyph_anchors ( font_id = 101 , glyph_name = 'H' , layer_name = 'Regular' , anchors = [{ 'name' : 'top' , 'x' : 320 , 'y' : 700 , 'cloud_enabled' : True , 'mark_enabled' : True }]) Source: FontLab MCP specification
title: fontpr.set_glyph_anchors

text: set_glyph_metrics ( * , glyph_name : str , lsb : float | None = None , rsb : float | None = None , advance_width : float | None = None , metrics_left : str | None = None , metrics_right : str | None = None , metrics_width : str | None = None , font_id : int | None = None , font_name : str | None = None ) -> Any Set glyph metrics on the active or requested glyph. Use numeric lsb/rsb/advance_width for direct edits, or metrics_left/metrics_right/metrics_width for expression-based metrics. Parameters: glyph_name (str, required): Glyph name. lsb (float, optional): Left sidebearing. rsb (float, optional): Right sidebearing. advance_width (float, optional): Advance width. metrics_left (str, optional): Metrics-left expression, for example 20 or =H. metrics_right (str, optional): Metrics-right expression. metrics_width (str, optional): Metrics-width expression. font_id (float, optional): Optional FontLab package id. font_name (str, optional): Optional font name match. Effect: glyph mutation with Undo. Returns: {status:"ok",glyph_metrics} Notes: At least one metric field is needed. Expressions apply first, then numeric LSB/RSB, then advance_width. Prefer separate calls/readback rather than conflicting expressions/numbers. Example expression: metrics_left:"=H" on a different glyph. This tool has no layer_name selector. # Example result = fontpr . set_glyph_metrics ( font_id = 101 , glyph_name = 'H' , advance_width = 640 ) Source: FontLab MCP specification
title: fontpr.set_glyph_metrics

text: set_kerning_class ( * , class_name : str , glyph_names : list [ Any ] | None = None , add_glyph_names : list [ Any ] | None = None , remove_glyph_names : list [ Any ] | None = None , left : bool | None = None , right : bool | None = None , font_id : int | None = None , font_name : str | None = None , master_name : str | None = None , undo : bool | None = None ) -> Any Create or update a kerning class on a font master. Use class_name without the @ prefix. Provide glyph_names to replace membership, or add_glyph_names/remove_glyph_names for incremental edits. Set left and/or right to control which side the class applies to. Parameters: class_name (str, required): Kerning class name without @ prefix. glyph_names (list[Any], optional): Optional glyph names that replace the full class membership. add_glyph_names (list[Any], optional): Optional glyph names to add to the class. remove_glyph_names (list[Any], optional): Optional glyph names to remove from the class. left (bool, optional): Whether the class applies on the left side. right (bool, optional): Whether the class applies on the right side. font_id (float, optional): Optional FontLab package id. font_name (str, optional): Optional font name match. master_name (str, optional): Optional master/layer name. Defaults to active master. undo (bool, optional): Create undo history. Default true. Effect: kerning mutation; undo defaults true. Destructive. Returns: {status,created,master,class:kerning_class} Notes: Create needs nonempty glyph_names or add_glyph_names naming existing glyphs; left/right each default true for creation and at least one must be true. Existing membership: glyph_names replaces everything and takes precedence over incremental add/remove arrays. Without it, removals happen before additions. Omitted side flags preserve existing sides. Creation, side flags and membership edits target the resolved master and restore the previously active master. Membership inputs are validated before side flags change; names must be nonempty strings naming existing glyphs. # Example result = fontpr . set_kerning_class ( font_id = 101 , class_name = 'A_Left' , glyph_names = [ 'A' , 'Aacute' ], left = True , right = False ) Source: FontLab MCP specification
title: fontpr.set_kerning_class

text: set_kerning_pair ( * , left : str , right : str , value : float , font_id : int | None = None , font_name : str | None = None , master_name : str | None = None , undo : bool | None = None ) -> Any Set the kerning value for a left/right pair on a font master. Use @GroupName for kerning classes. Parameters: left (str, required): Left glyph name or @class. right (str, required): Right glyph name or @class. value (float, required): Kerning value. font_id (float, optional): Optional FontLab package id. font_name (str, optional): Optional font name match. master_name (str, optional): Optional master/layer name. Defaults to active master. undo (bool, optional): Create undo history. Default true. Effect: kerning mutation; undo defaults true. Returns: {status,master,left,right,value} Notes: master_name resolves the target master; the write and its Undo/Redo retain that master without changing the active one. Read back with get_kerning_pair. value must be a JSON number. # Example result = fontpr . set_kerning_pair ( font_id = 101 , left = 'A' , right = 'V' , value =- 80 ) Source: FontLab MCP specification
title: fontpr.set_kerning_pair

text: set_preferences ( * , patch : dict [ str , Any ]) -> Any Patch FontLab application preferences using exact keys and value types from get_preferences. Persists changes and refreshes preference listeners. Validate meaning and enum/range constraints with explain first. Some settings require a restart. Credentials and unsupported keys cannot be changed. Preferences are not part of font Undo. Parameters: patch (dict[str, Any], required): Non-empty mapping of exact preference keys to new values. Points use {x,y}; string lists use arrays of strings. Effect: persistent application mutation. Returns: {preferences:{key:appliedValue},persisted:true,note} Notes: Discover the key/value/type and enum meaning first; this illustrative key is not an instruction to change save policy. The entire patch is validated for known keys/types first. Values may normalize; persistence or readback errors can occur after in-memory changes. No font Undo. # Example result = fontpr . set_preferences ( patch = { 'font.ask_file_name' : 2 }) Source: FontLab MCP specification

text: write_aidus_file ( * , root : str , path : str , content : str , overwrite : bool | None = None ) -> Any Create or replace a UTF-8 text file only in Aidus or Scripts/Aidus under FontLab's user data folder. No Python or open font required. Creates missing parent folders. Relative paths only; traversal and symbolic links rejected. At most 256 KiB. Existing files require overwrite=true; read them first. New files use exclusive creation; replacements use atomic save. Returns absolute_path, bytes and sha256 after successful writing. Does not execute scripts. File writes are outside font Undo. Parameters: root (str, required; one of aidus , scripts ): aidus for output/data; scripts for Python scripts. path (str, required): Nonempty relative file path, with '/' separators, e.g. reports/glyphs.txt or generate.py. content (str, required): Complete UTF-8 text to save. Empty files are allowed; NUL and binary data are not. overwrite (bool, optional): Explicitly replace an existing regular file. Default false. Effect: write file; outside font Undo. Returns: {status,root,path,absolute_path,bytes,sha256,replaced} Notes: No Python or open font needed. Uses the configured FontLab user data directory (default if unset), which must already exist; creates Aidus subfolders and parent directories on demand. UTF-8 text only, up to 256 KiB. Missing files are exclusively created; replacement requires overwrite=true and uses QSaveFile atomic commit. Cannot replace directories or symlinks. Read an existing file before replacing it. No append, delete, binary-file support, arbitrary root, or script execution is provided by these tools. File changes are not part of font Undo. The path restrictions apply to these tools; separately authorized run_python still uses the normal Python environment. # Save a script without executing it result = fontpr . write_aidus_file ( root = 'scripts' , path = 'generate.py' , content = 'print("Hello from Aidus") \n ' ) Source: FontLab MCP specification

text: PySide2 keyword arguments for native PythonQt calls, which reject every keyword. QLabel("x", parent=w) raises "called slot does not support kwargs" in FontLab's PythonQt (pqs-g04/probe_keywords.json). The generated _keywords.json lists the PySide2 parameter names of each routed constructor and method overload. A keyword call becomes a positional one when exactly one positional form fits; a skipped parameter needs a recorded Qt declaration default. Constructor keywords that name no parameter set a Qt property or connect a signal after construction, as PySide2 does. Anything ambiguous or unmapped keeps the native call, and its native error. The table loads on the first call that actually passes keywords.

text: slot_forwarder ( slot : Any ) -> Callable Connect a native slot through a Python function. text: pyside_method ( obj : Any , name : str ) -> Any Return obj.name as PySide2 code would call it, without altering obj . Native Qt properties confirmed by metaObject().indexOfProperty() become zero-argument getters. Measured out-parameter methods listed in _out_parameters.json return PySide2's (value, ok) tuple: QTransform/QMatrix inverted() via the native isInvertible() , and 37 others ( QLocale.toInt , QInputDialog.getText and so on) by passing a native PythonQt.BoolResult in the out-parameter slot. Pass obj as the class for static methods. Keyword calls and calls that already pass a BoolResult stay native. Methods listed in _implicit_conversions.json wrap a measured native enum argument as PySide2's implicit value class ( setEasingCurve(QEasingCurve.OutElastic) passes QEasingCurve(OutElastic) ); plain ints and other values pass through. Keyword arguments, which PythonQt rejects on every native method, are mapped to positions by the PySide2 parameter names in _keywords.json . Everything else is the ordinary attribute. The same rules apply to calls in sources run with run_app .

text: Delta Machine calculator: Input value and Desired value per input -> Percent through the Delta Machine, with no glyph and no font (dm_percent_desired; dm_percent / dm_value: one wanted value, or a percent). A value (a distance in units: a sidebearing, an advance, a stem, a counter...) is typed per input of an axis. The Delta Machine moves it as it moves any distance of an outline: interpolated at the target stem, then scaled with the stems preserved (compensation 0). With compensation 0 the result is affine in the scale, not proportional: d(s) = d_t + (s - 1) * (d_heavy - b * d_t) / (1 - b) d_t: the value at the target stem (= the result at 100 %); d_heavy: the value on the heavier input of the segment; b: heavier input stem / target stem. So the percent that gives a wanted value is not wanted / d_t (the plain ratio) unless the value is the same on every input. A value that changes like the stem (d_heavy / d_t = b) does not change with the scale. The math is the core Delta itself, not a copy: a two-point DeltaScale (0 and the value, per input) is driven by DeltaScale.scale_by_stem and the percent is solved by delta_panel_actions._solve_scale (the solver of the units sizes) with a signed measure. Axes with more inputs and extrapolation work as in the bake. Desired values per input (a client's sidebearings for each master): the wanted value on the target is the desired values interpolated at the target stem (the same DeltaScale at 100 %), then solved as above. Affine metrics (Delta Machine default since 2026-11-06, Advanced > Delta metrics off): a Met. W percent multiplies the sidebearings interpolated at the target stem, so its percent is the plain ratio (affine_percent). Width / Height stay Delta Machine percents. Host neutral; nothing is written anywhere.

text: Delta Machine kerning: the kerning of a target layer from its axis inputs. Kerning rides the same axis as the outlines. Per pair and per baked side: the inputs' values are interpolated at the side's V stem on the side's axis (piecewise linear, as the Delta engine reads the stems; a pair missing in an input counts as 0), then scaled by the mean of the two sides' factors (side_factor: the outline width scale, and a kerning spacing looser than the outline loosens the pair in inverse ratio, a tighter one tightens it; the kerning spacing is the row's Kern % when set, else Met. W): k = mean(k_left_axis(t_left), k_right_axis(t_right)) * (f_left + f_right) / 2 Host neutral. A kerning table is {(left, right): value}; a key that starts with '@' is a kerning group (the side follows from its place in the pair), any other key is a glyph (an exception). The host translates its own keys (Glyphs: @MMK_L_ / @MMK_R_, glyph ids). Groups are used as given: this module never adds, renames or removes a group. Rules (Delta Machine Advanced, user 2026-10-26): - group rule, a group whose baked members differ (rows / sizes): mean (default) | key (the member named like the group, else the first baked member) | refuse (the pair is not written, the group is reported); - side rule, a pair side with no baked glyph (glyph in no row, or a row with Kern off): complete (default; factor 1, the pair is still computed, so the master is complete) | skip (only pairs with both sides baked are written; others are removed from the target) | keep (the target's own value stays; for a new / lib target the same as skip). Pairs in the target that no input has are the user's own: never touched. LTR only (RTL and vertical: later).

text: Delta Machine: stem-driven interpolation targets per glyph group. The Delta Machine bakes target layers from virtual axes, like the Delta panel's Bake, but each target row also names a glyph group, so one layer can get different stems and sizes for different glyphs (Vassil for the lowercase with one set of values, Vassil for the uppercase with another). Axes and targets are apart (format 5): an axis is a set of input layers with their stems (Weight lc: Regular 80 / Bold 160), a target row names the axis it is computed from, so the lowercase and the capitals of one layer can use different axes. A row without a group works on the selected glyphs. A row may name several groups, or All groups (every group of the document, also groups added later); an override row under it changes the values for one of its groups and inherits the cells it leaves empty (format 4). Width and height are in percent (default) or in units, each on its own: 60 % wide and exactly 700 units high is one row. Units are measured on the group's reference glyph when it has one (the scale found there is used for the whole group, so overshoots and descenders keep their proportions), else on each glyph. This module is host neutral: the document (normalize, validate), unit parsing, machine_expand (rows -> one resolved row per group, overrides first) and the plan that turns the rows into one core Delta setup per glyph (delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_bake / npa_delta_solve_target).

text: Design space plan: axes and masters, edited away from the font and applied in one step (Delta Machine, Designspace tab). Axes are defined as in FontLab (name, tag, minimum / default / maximum) and may be driven: the coordinate of a master on a driven axis comes from its stems or its width / height percent in the Delta setup, so a Weight axis can simply be the V stem. Masters are rows with one coordinate per axis; a master is in the font, new (empty, copy of a master, or made from a Delta target layer), or marked for removal. Host neutral. The host reads the font into a plan (axes / masters with their font ids), the user edits it, plan_diff() lists what applying would change, the host applies it. Plan shape: {'axes': [{'key', 'id', 'name', 'tag', 'min', 'default', 'max', 'driver', 'hidden'}], 'masters': [{'key', 'id', 'name', 'source': {'kind', 'from'}, 'location': {axis key: float}, 'default': bool, 'remove': bool}]} axis 'key' / master 'key': stable within the plan (renames keep them); 'id': the font's axisId / master id ('' = not in the font yet); source kind: 'font' (in the font), 'copy' (from: master name), 'target' (from: target layer name; the layers of every glyph are copied), 'empty'; driver: see DRIVERS.

text: Glyph groups: auto sort, export for an agent, import with a coverage check. Delta Machine groups (Uppercase, Lowercase, Small caps, ...) decide which target settings a glyph gets. A glyph in no group is never baked by a named row, so every operation here accounts for every glyph of the font: auto_groups(records) every glyph into one group by its Glyphs category / case / name suffix; the rest into Uncategorized groups_export(records, groups) the groups + Uncategorized (glyphs in no group) + a read-only glyph table (Unicode, character, category, case, script, components, OpenType features / classes, auto group) + instructions for an agent that sorts them by name; groups_dump() writes it one glyph per line groups_import(raw, font_names) groups back from that file (or a plain {group: [names]}); names not in the font are dropped, font glyphs the file misses go to Uncategorized; a report says so Glyph records are host neutral dicts (the host fills them, Glyphs: gs3/gui/glyph_filters.glyph_record): {'name', 'unicodes': ['0061'], 'category', 'subCategory', 'case', 'script', 'export', 'shape': outline | composite | mixed | empty, 'components': [names]} Missing keys are empty.

text: contour_align ( contours , mode = 'CC' , align_x = 'C' , align_y = 'E' , layer_bounds = None , target_node = None , contours_A = None , contours_B = None ) Align contours to each other or to a computed target. Arguments: contours (list[Contour]): Contours to align (CC/CL/CN modes). mode (str): Alignment mode. One of: 'CC' - Contour to contour (pairwise or to selection bounds). 'CL' - Contour to layer bounding box (pass layer_bounds ). 'CN' - Contour to a target node (pass target_node ); the first contour in contours is assumed to host the target and is excluded from the move. 'AB' - Group A to group B (pass contours_A , contours_B ); group A is shifted as a whole so that its origin lands on group B's origin. align_x (str): 'L' / 'R' / 'C' / 'K' (keep). align_y (str): 'B' / 'T' / 'E' / 'X' (keep). layer_bounds (Bounds|None): required for mode='CL'. target_node (Node|Point|tuple|None): required for mode='CN'. contours_A (list[Contour]|None): required for mode='AB'. contours_B (list[Contour]|None): required for mode='AB'. Returns: bool: True if any contours were moved.

Analyse the first scope layer once, then cut every scope layer node-exact, all or nothing. The first entry in scope_layers is the analysis (reference) layer. Selection on it (per-contour) drives which contours are cut; with no selection, all contours are. Cut endpoints are planned once on the reference (plan_cut_nodes) and inserted as nodes at the same (contour, segment, t) on every layer, so no distance snap can diverge between masters. text: lock_directions ( layer , plan , slope , vstem = None ) Italic fix on a baked core layer (changed in place), switched by the plan (_italic_plan): re-extremize ('keep_extremes'; 'balanced': search a balanced position when the exact move misses 'fit_tol'), lock the labelled handles, restore tension ('keep_tension', needs vstem; 'tension_on_rebuilt', 'tension_scale'). Vertical lock: x = node x (Y kept); slant: back on the slant line through the node (Y kept); horizontal: y = node y. A smooth node with one locked handle turns its other handle in line (length kept). Returns a report {'locked', 'drift', 'extremes', 'balanced', 'fit_error', 'fallbacks', 'tension', 'errors'}. Fallback chain (nothing here stops a bake): a fit that raises is "no fit" (balanced sample skipped / exact merge -> balanced search); an extreme that raises keeps its node and gets the lock only (a fallback); a curve whose tension raises keeps its handles. 'errors' lists what was caught. _scale_layer goes one step further: if the whole fix raises, the layer is plain Delta.
title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.lock_directions

text: npa_delta_bake ( glyph , scope_layers , NodeActions , setup_json ) Bake all targets across all axes in the supplied setup against the active glyph. Returns a JSON-serialisable status dict. scope_layers is ignored — Delta operates over the layers named in the setup, not over the layer-mode scope. The host is expected to keep glyph current. A target may carry its own 'metrics' / 'anchors' (bool, default: the option); when off, that attribute is left out of the entry's 'viable' and the target layer keeps its own metrics / anchors.

title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_live_clear

text: npa_delta_live_drive ( glyph , scope_layers , NodeActions , target_name , vstem , hstem , sx , sy , origin = None ) Drive the named layer on the live glyph from the cached snapshot. The snapshot was captured by the most recent npa_delta_live_set. Reading from the snapshot — not from the live glyph — is what prevents the cascade (each tick computes from the original frozen inputs). origin: optional transform-origin code for this call (see _ORIGIN_FROM_CODE); None keeps the snapshot's options.origin. Whole layer: the result's origin point lands on the same point of the base input's bounds. Selection mode: on the same point of the current selection bounds (BS: no realignment).
title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_live_drive

text: npa_delta_live_set ( glyph , scope_layers , NodeActions , setup_json , selection_layer = None ) Snapshot the input layers of the Live Axis and pre-build the DeltaScale dict. Subsequent npa_delta_live_drive calls operate on this frozen snapshot — they never re-read from the host glyph, so driving the active layer doesn't feed back into the deltas. The setup_json shape matches the bake setup but is expected to contain exactly one axis (the Live Axis) and no real targets. Selection mode (options.selection and selection_layer given): the snapshot covers only the nodes selected on selection_layer (the host's active layer). Each input's point_array is sliced by those indices and a DeltaScale is built from the slices — filter at the snapshot, not at the write. Nothing selected -> whole layer. Geometry only: metrics and anchors are not driven in this mode.
title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_live_set

title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_master_names

text: npa_delta_measure_stem ( glyph , scope_layers , NodeActions , layer_name , axis ) Measure |Δ| along axis ('x' or 'y') between the first and last selected on-curve nodes on layer_name. Returns a float or None. The host sets node.selected before this call (FontRig's syncToPython does it; the FL panel reads its own live selection differently).
title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_measure_stem

text: npa_delta_measure_stems_all ( glyph , scope_layers , NodeActions , axis ) Compatibility-aware stem measurement across every layer of the glyph. Finds the index pair from whichever layer carries the live selection (host-side selection is single-layer in FontRig; in FL this still works because the active layer carries the selection), then looks up those same indices on every other layer and returns {layer_name: float_or_None} as a JSON string. The host (JS or FL) picks the values it cares about for the rows it has and silently skips layers where the index pair doesn't exist (incompatible / different topology).
title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_measure_stems_all

text: npa_delta_solve_target ( glyph , scope_layers , NodeActions , setup_json ) Solve the scales of every mixed-mode target on this glyph without writing anything: the first pass of a reference-glyph bake (solve on H, then bake the whole group with these percentages). Returns {'ok', 'scales': [{'axis', 'name', 'sx', 'sy', 'converged', 'residual'}], 'warnings'}; sx / sy in percent. Stems targets echo their own sx / sy; dimensions targets are skipped.
title: typerig.core.actions.delta_panel_actions.npa_delta_solve_target

text: cap_angular ( contour , idx_a , idx_b ) Build a pointed (miter) cap between two stem-corner nodes. Extends the two stem tangents from A and B until they intersect; the intersection becomes the cap tip. Single sharp on-curve replacing any existing cap interior. Returns None if the tangents are parallel (no well-defined tip). Arguments: contour : Contour idx_a : int — first stem corner idx_b : int — second stem corner Returns: Node or None — the tip on-curve.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.cap_angular

text: cap_butt ( contour , idx_a , idx_b , side = 'auto' ) Build a perpendicular flat (butt) cap between two stem-corner nodes. Drops a perpendicular from one corner onto the opposite stem segment. The new on-curve replaces both A and B and any nodes between them; the surviving stem segment on the kept side is split at the perpendicular foot. Arguments: contour : Contour idx_a : int — first stem corner (cap region begins after A in contour order) idx_b : int — second stem corner (cap region ends at B in contour order) side : 'a' | 'b' | 'auto' — which stem to keep. 'a' projects from B onto the segment behind A (keeps prev_on(A) intact and clean-cuts seg_in_a). 'b' projects from A onto the segment ahead of B (keeps next_on(B) intact and clean-cuts seg_out_b). 'auto' picks the side whose perpendicular foot lies closer to the opposite corner — i.e. the shorter cut. Returns: Node or None — the inserted on-curve replacing the cap, or None on failure.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.cap_butt

text: cap_rebuild ( contour , node_indices , target = 'butt' ) Universal "flatten an existing cap" — collapses any cap region back to a straight butt cut. Detects the two boundary on-curves at the ends of the selection range (these are the cap-corner stem ends), then runs cap_butt against them. Works on any contiguous selection — the previous fixed-7-node restriction of the FL implementation is gone. Arguments: contour : Contour node_indices : iterable[int] — indices of selected nodes inside the cap target : str — only 'butt' is implemented currently. Reserved for future 'round'/'angular' rebuild targets. Returns: Node or None — the new on-curve replacing the cap, or None on failure.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.cap_rebuild

text: cap_round ( contour , idx_a , idx_b , curvature = 1.0 , keep_length = False ) Build an italic-aware circular cap between two stem-corner nodes. Two placement modes: * keep_length=False (default) — the cap extends OUTWARD past the chord A-B by radius r along the stem axis. The original stems are kept intact and the round cap adds length to the overall path. The tip sits on the circle of radius |AB|/2 centred at midpoint(A,B), in the outward stem direction. * keep_length=True — the cap fits INSIDE the original stems. Each stem segment is shortened by r so the new corners A', B' sit at distance r INSIDE the original A, B along the stem. Overall path length is preserved (matches original FL cap_round behavior). Italic-aware in both modes: the cap tip lies along the averaged stem axis, not the chord-perpendicular. See compute_cap_round_arc. Arguments: contour : Contour idx_a : int — first stem corner idx_b : int — second stem corner curvature : float — handle-length multiplier (1.0 = true circle). keep_length : bool — preserve overall path length (FL behaviour). Returns: Node or None — the tip on-curve, or None on failure.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.cap_round

text: corner_rebuild ( contour , node_indices , cleanup = True ) Collapse a rounded or multi-node corner back to a cusp. The selection brackets the corner: of the two outermost selected on-curve nodes, the one before the corner keeps the incoming side and the one after it keeps the outgoing side. Both sides are run out along their own geometry until they cross, and everything in between is dropped. Which node is which is worked out from the contour, so the tool does not care where the contour's start point sits. Either side may be a line or a curve. For LL--CC--AA the result is LL--AA meeting at the crossing of the line projection with the arc continuation; AA keeps the curvature it had before the corner was rounded, its handles recomputed by de Casteljau splitting at the solved time rather than straightened. Arguments: contour (Contour): The contour to operate on. node_indices (list[int]): Indices of selected nodes (must include at least 2 on-curve nodes that bracket the corner region). cleanup (bool): If True, remove the corner nodes after collapsing. If False, only pull the selection onto the cusp. Returns: bool: True if the corner was rebuilt.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.corner_rebuild

text: make_collinear ( contour , node_indices , mode =- 1 , equalize = False , target_width = None , snap_to = None , snap_tolerance = 0.25 ) Align two selected curve segments to be collinear at their handle directions — typically the two parallel-stem-side curves of a stem so the stem starts and ends straight. Selection model: - A "selected curve" is an on-curve A whose forward segment is a CubicBezier, and whose 4 segment nodes (A, bcp_out, bcp_in, next_on) are ALL in node_indices. - Exactly 2 selected curves are required. With 0, 1, or 3+, the operation returns 0 (no-op). - The walk uses contour.nodes order, so a selection that wraps past the contour start is handled correctly (no hash-dedup, no first-and-last heuristic — the previous bug source). Direction swapping is delegated to CubicBezier.make_collinear, which uses match_direction_to to detect and handle parallel-stem curves drawn in opposite contour directions. Arguments: contour : Contour node_indices : iterable[int] — selected node indices mode : int — 0 = lock to first selected curve, 1 = lock to second, -1 = average (default) equalize : bool — equalize stem width to target_width target_width : float | None — width for equalize; None = current average Returns: int — number of curve pairs aligned (0 or 1).
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.make_collinear

text: make_monoline ( contour , node_indices , target_width = None , preserve_taper = False , snap_to = None , snap_tolerance = 0.25 ) Regularize two selected curve segments as +/- offsets of their shared control-polygon median (monoline-pen model). Selection model is identical to make_collinear: exactly 2 selected curves, each consisting of A, bcp_out, bcp_in, next_on all in node_indices. Returns 0 (no-op) for any other selection count. Direction swapping is delegated to CubicBezier.make_monoline, which uses match_direction_to to handle parallel-stem curves drawn in opposite contour directions. Arguments: contour : Contour node_indices : iterable[int] - selected node indices target_width : float | None - uniform stem width; None = average of the perpendicular widths measured at the two endpoints preserve_taper : bool - if True, keep separate widths at each end Returns: int - number of curve pairs aligned (0 or 1).

text: nodes_align ( nodes , mode = 'L' , smart_shift = True , keep_relations = False , lerp_shift = False , intercept = False , extrapolate = False , target = None ) Align nodes to a computed target based on the alignment mode. Arguments: nodes (list[Node]): The nodes to align. mode (str): Alignment mode. One of: 'L' - Align to leftmost X 'R' - Align to rightmost X 'T' - Align to topmost Y 'B' - Align to bottommost Y 'C' - Align to horizontal center of selection 'E' - Align to vertical center of selection 'BBoxCenterX' - Align to X center of bounding box 'BBoxCenterY' - Align to Y center of bounding box 'peerCenterX' - Align each node to midpoint of its prev/next on-curve X 'peerCenterY' - Align each node to midpoint of its prev/next on-curve Y 'Y' - Align to imaginary line between Y-min and Y-max of selection (project X) 'X' - Align to imaginary line between X-min and X-max of selection (project Y) smart_shift (bool): If True, dragging an on-curve also drags adjacent BCPs. If False, only the on-curve coordinate moves ("dumb shift"). keep_relations (bool): If True, treat selection as a rigid group: compute one delta from group anchor to target and shift every node uniformly, preserving relative offsets between selected nodes. With a target the anchor is the bounding-box side the mode names (L / R / T / B, centre for C / E and the rest); without one it is the selection's mean. lerp_shift (bool): If True, use Interpolated Nudge (Node.lerp_shift) instead of direct relocation. Mutually exclusive with intercept and extrapolate. intercept (bool): If True, for vertical modes (T/B/E) project each node's X onto the line through its prev/next on-curve neighbours so it slides along the local stem. Mutually exclusive with lerp_shift and extrapolate. extrapolate (bool): If True, slide on-curve nodes along their cubic bezier (or its mathematical extension) instead of moving by coordinate. Mutually exclusive with lerp_shift and intercept. target (Point|Node|None): If provided, overrides the mode-computed target. Modes still control which axis (X / Y / both) is applied. Returns: bool: True if any nodes were moved.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_actions.NodeActions.nodes_align

text: npa_contour_bool ( glyph , scope_layers , operation = 'add' , reverse = False ) Boolean operation on selected contours (all if none) - FL contour_bool. The operands are read ONCE on a reference layer (the active layer if in scope, else the first) and applied by contour index to every layer in scope: Glyphs keeps a separate selection per layer, so other masters have none to read. Left fold in index order (reverse: from the last, FL Alt); the result takes the place of the base operand. Open contours are not operands and stay. Layers whose contour count differs from the reference are skipped and reported; results that differ in node structure across layers are reported (no fix). The geometry is the host's: each layer must offer path_boolean(indices, operation, reverse) -> (status, new_paths, message) (Glyphs: trLayer.path_boolean, engine proxy/gs3/objects/pathops). Args: operation (str): 'add', 'subtract', 'intersect' or 'exclude'. reverse (bool): fold from the last operand. Returns: dict: layer name -> status ('OK', 'EMPTY', 'TOO_FEW', 'BAD_INDEX', 'ENGINE_ERROR', 'INCOMPATIBLE', 'NO_HOST'). Empty if nothing ran.
title: typerig.core.actions.node_panel_actions.npa_contour_bool

text: MAT-graph-based skeleton extraction. Traces each topological stroke of a glyph as a single Bezier contour running along the medial axis. Strokes that meet at L-corners (e.g. the frame of 'E') are walked as one continuous path; strokes that meet at T-junctions (e.g. the middle arm of 'E', the stem-into- bar of 'T') are split into separate contours. Pure closed loops (O, D, rounded frames) emit one closed contour. Node positions are MAT-graph positions (fork/terminal nodes + DP- retained knots at curvature bends), not source-node projections. Short corner-bisector "leg" branches at convex outline corners are dropped at the graph level so L-corners collapse into pass-throughs. Reuses: - compute_mat — graph + radii - extract_stroke_paths — tangent-continuing path walker (from stroke_sep_mat ) - _simplify_branch — Douglas-Peucker Each output on-curve node carries node.lib['radius'] = half the local stroke width at that point.

text: General N-contour planar slicer for the StrokeSep pipeline. Given a scene of contours and a list of cross-contour cuts, this module constructs the planar graph formed by contour arcs (the on-curve segments between cut endpoints) and cut edges (the connectors themselves), walks the graph's faces using a standard half-edge / next-CW-at-vertex rule, and returns each interior face as an output Contour piece. This replaces the pair-by-pair _slice_frame dispatch that fails when three or more contours share cross-cuts (B: outer + 2 bowl counters; uni5C4A: outer + many inner counters). The pair-by-pair approach operated on stale copies of a shared contour across iterations, producing overlapping/spurious geometry. The planar-face approach treats every involved contour exactly once.
title: typerig.core.algo.stroke_sep_slicer

text: Snap each cut endpoint to the nearest on-curve node across all contours. For each involved contour, sort its cut endpoints by on-curve index and build one forward+one reverse half-edge (arc) per consecutive pair. Arcs preserve the off-curve handles between their on-curve endpoints. For each cut, build a forward+reverse half-edge (cut). At every vertex, sort outgoing half-edges by direction angle (CCW). Set he.next = the half-edge at he.dest that is immediately CW before he.twin in the sorted list (standard planar face-walking rule — walks each face on its left side). Walk faces; skip faces bounded entirely by arcs from a single contour (those are the plane's outer face and inner-counter "hole" interiors). Return the remaining faces as closed Contour objects.
title: Algorithm (summary)

text: capture ( key , measured ) Capture lookup for a given measurement. If measured falls inside ANY target's band under key , returns (target, signed_correction) where signed_correction = target.value - measured. If multiple bands overlap and capture the same value, the target whose .value is closest wins; ties go to the earlier declaration. Out-of-band measurements (in no target's capture window) return None — the allowlist makes no claim on them. Empty / missing key returns None.

text: boundary_ratio ( marg , face , idc ) Measured split of a ⿰ / ⿱ glyph as a fraction of the FACE, or None. marg : (col, row) marginals of the glyph raster (see marginals()). face : (c0, r0, c1, r1) face extent in image coords (see face_frame()). idc : '⿰' -> left-part width fraction (0..1 across the face width); '⿱' -> top-part height fraction (0..1 down the face height). Uses the positional valley_split_face inside the face window so it locates the real component gap even when one part carries far more ink. Returns None when there is no clean valley or it falls outside the face core (<=0.05 or =0.95). This is the single implementation shared by the per-glyph Measure and the whole-font zones scan.

Passed in so the caller controls the raster source. frame : (x0, y0, x1, y1) em-square band. groups : list[list[contour_index]] by component, for the second-line gauge. Centroid offsets are normalized by band width/height; mesh separators and face rates are already fractions; D is normalized by span; M is dimensionless. This makes every gauge directly comparable across glyphs for family/anchor bands and live z-scores.

A real CJK face fills most of the em; a leftover stroke on a glyph you are still building is a small fraction of it. text: rasterize_contours ( contours , frame , S , samples = 4 ) Antialiased raster of flattened contours over the em-square frame. contours : list[list[(x, y)]] - closed polygons in font units. frame : (x0, y0, x1, y1) font-space band mapped onto the S x S image. S : raster edge length. samples : vertical sub-scanlines per pixel row for AA (horizontal coverage is analytic, so this only refines the y axis). returns : flat list[float] of length S*S, ink = 0..255, row-major with the TOP image row first (row 0 == the ascender / y1). text: Curvilinear Shape Feature descriptor (Berio et al. 2022, §4.2). A CSF captures a curvature extremum on the glyph outline. Taken together, the CSFs of a glyph FULLY COVER the outline — adjacent CSFs share exactly one support segment with no gaps between them. Attributes: csf_type: 'convex' (from M terminal) or 'concave' (from M* terminal) disk_center: (x, y) — inscribed-circle center of the terminal disk disk_radius: float — disk radius = min distance to outline contact_region: list of (x, y) — outline sample points inside the disk arc extremum: (x, y) — midpoint of the contact region; canonical CSF position axis: list of (x, y) — local symmetry axis from terminal toward fork support_segments:(left_pts, right_pts) — outline arcs on each side of contact contour_idx: int — which input contour this CSF belongs to arc_param: float — arc-length s of extremum (used for ordering) arc_start: float — arc-length start of contact region arc_end: float — arc-length end of contact region Concave-only attributes (populated by compute_csfs): tangent_pair: ((tx, ty), (tx', ty')) — unit tangents at contact endpoints inward_normal: (nx, ny) — -(τ + τ') normalised, pointing toward extremum

text: compute_csfs ( contours , mat_graph , exterior_terminals , sample_step = 3.0 , tau_c = _TAU_C , max_passes = 3 ) Compute Curvilinear Shape Features (CSFs) for a glyph. Two-pass algorithm (Berio et al. §4.2): Pass 1: Create initial CSFs from M terminals (convex) and M* terminals (concave). These capture the major outline features. Pass 2+: Iteratively search each support segment for additional CSFs that the medial axes missed (smooth curves, slight concavities). New concave CSFs are accepted only if radius < τ_c × glyph_height. Spiral artifacts (Tait-Kneser) are discarded. The returned CSFs fully cover the outline: adjacent CSFs share one support segment, with no gaps. Args: contours: list of TypeRig Contour objects (the glyph outline) mat_graph: MATGraph from compute_mat() — interior medial axis M exterior_terminals: list of (x, y, radius, cx, cy) from compute_exterior_mat() — exterior medial axis M* terminals that touch the outline sample_step: outline sampling density in font units (default 3.0) tau_c: radius threshold for new concave CSFs as fraction of glyph height (paper default: 0.15) max_passes: maximum iterative refinement passes (default: 3) Returns: list of CSF objects
title: typerig.core.algo.csf.compute_csfs

text: apply_transfer ( tgt_points , xform , residual_norm = None , tgt_bbox = None , src_bbox = None , src_centroid = None , dst_centroid = None , tgt_centroid = None , mode = 'affine_residual' ) Apply a fitted design change to a target contour. The fitted affine represents the change "src becomes dst". We do NOT apply it to tgt in absolute coordinates - that would drag tgt toward src's world position. Instead we pivot the linear part of the affine at tgt's own centroid and add the inter-centroid translation on top. Let L be the 2x2 linear block and c_s, c_d, c_t the src/dst/tgt centroids; for each target point t: t_new = L * (t - c_t) + c_t + (c_d - c_s) + residual_term residual_term is the per-point residual from compute_residual, rescaled from src bbox units to tgt bbox units per axis. Modes: 'affine_only' - skip residual even if supplied 'affine_residual' - apply L + centroid delta + residual (default) 'bbox_fallback' - mimic the legacy rigid-body path: use only diagonal of L (scale_x, scale_y) and centroid delta; no rotation, no shear, no residual Args: tgt_points: iterable of (x, y) or Point xform: Transform from fit_affine (src -> dst) residual_norm: output of compute_residual, or None tgt_bbox, src_bbox: Bounds; used only for residual rescaling src_centroid, dst_centroid: (x, y); if supplied, the centroid delta is c_d - c_s exactly. If omitted, delta is reconstructed from the fit's translation using src_bbox centre as a proxy for c_s - accurate for symmetric contours; prefer the explicit form for asymmetric shapes. tgt_centroid: (x, y); if omitted, computed from tgt_points. mode: see above
title: typerig.core.algo.design_transfer.apply_transfer

text: compute_residual ( src_points , dst_points , xform , src_bbox = None ) Per-point leftover after affine prediction, normalised by src bbox. Residual_i = (dst_i - A(src_i)) / (src_bbox.width, src_bbox.height) Normalising to unit space lets the residual be reapplied on a target contour of different size by rescaling with the target's bbox extent (see apply_transfer). Zero bbox extent on an axis disables residual on that axis. Args: src_points: iterable of (x, y) or Point dst_points: same length as src_points xform: Transform from fit_affine src_bbox: optional precomputed Bounds over src_points Returns: list of (rx, ry) tuples in unit space, length len(src_points)
title: typerig.core.algo.design_transfer.compute_residual

text: decompose_affine ( xform ) Decompose an affine's linear part via polar decomposition. The linear 2x2 block L is written R * S where R is a rotation and S is symmetric. Rotation angle, uniform + anisotropic scale, and shear are read off S. Values are advisory only - intended for UI feedback and for thresholding "is this close to a rigid motion?" decisions. Args: xform: Transform (typerig convention) Returns: dict with keys: rotation_deg - signed rotation angle extracted from R, degrees scale_x - diagonal of S in the first principal direction scale_y - diagonal of S in the second principal direction shear - off-diagonal of S normalised by avg scale determinant - det(L); negative means R is a reflection translation - (dx, dy)
title: typerig.core.algo.design_transfer.decompose_affine

text: fit_affine ( src_points , dst_points ) Least-squares 2D affine fit, src -> dst. Fits parameters (xx, xy, yx, yy, dx, dy) of the typerig Transform convention such that for each pair (sx, sy) -> (tx, ty): tx ~ xx * sx + yx * sy + dx ty ~ xy * sx + yy * sy + dy The two rows of the affine are independent 3-parameter regressions that share the same 3x3 Gram matrix G = sum over points of [[sx sx, sx sy, sx], [sy sx, sy sy, sy], [sx, sy, 1 ]] so we invert G once and apply it to two right-hand sides. Args: src_points: iterable of (x, y) or Point, length N >= 3 dst_points: iterable of (x, y) or Point, same length Returns: (Transform, rms_residual) Transform - fitted affine, typerig convention rms_residual - sqrt(mean(|dst - A(src)|^2)) in input units; 0 for perfectly affine pairs Raises: ValueError on length mismatch, fewer than 3 points, or a degenerate point configuration (all src points collinear).
title: typerig.core.algo.design_transfer.fit_affine

text: transfer_contour ( src_points , dst_points , tgt_points , mode = 'affine_residual' ) End-to-end per-contour transfer: fit src->dst, reproduce on tgt. This is the function intended for callers (e.g. FontLab scripts). Handles centroid extraction, bbox extraction, residual, and apply_transfer in one call. Args: src_points: iterable of (x, y) or Point - the OLD master state dst_points: same length - the NEW master state tgt_points: iterable of (x, y) or Point - the receiver contour mode: 'affine_only' | 'affine_residual' | 'bbox_fallback' Returns: (new_tgt_points, info) where new_tgt_points: list of (x, y) tuples, length == len(tgt_points) info: dict with diagnostic fields: rms_residual - affine fit quality (source units) max_residual - largest per-point residual magnitude (source units) - 0 if no residual computed rotation_deg, scale_x, scale_y, shear - from decompose_affine determinant - of the 2x2 linear part
title: typerig.core.algo.design_transfer.transfer_contour

text: curve_curve_intersections ( c1 , c2 , tolerance = 0.1 ) All intersections of two cubic beziers given as 4-point tuples ((x0,y0),(x1,y1),(x2,y2),(x3,y3)). Bezier clipping via recursive subdivision: disjoint control-polygon boxes prune the pair; when both boxes are smaller than tolerance in both dimensions the accumulated (t1, t2) interval midpoints are reported as a hit. Results whose t1 nearly coincide are merged. NOTE: overlapping-COINCIDENT curves (identical or sharing an arc) intersect everywhere; the depth cap makes the call terminate but the returned hits are an unspecified sample of the overlap region. Args: c1, c2 : 4-point tuple cubics tolerance : spatial precision of reported points (font units) Returns: list of (t1, t2, (x, y)) sorted by t1
title: typerig.core.algo.intersect.curve_curve_intersections

text: curve_curve_intersections_extended ( c1 , c2 , seeds = None , limit = 4.0 , tolerance = 1e-07 ) Intersections of two cubics WITHOUT clamping t to the segment. curve_curve_intersections() only reports crossings that lie inside both segments. Rebuilding a corner needs the crossing of the two curves' extensions past the region that was cut away, so this solves the 2x2 system F(t, u) = C1(t) - C2(u) = 0 with damped Newton-Raphson from a set of seeds. Bezier arithmetic extrapolates cleanly, so a solution with t > 1 or u < 0 is a genuine point on the analytic continuation of the curve and can be reached by de Casteljau splitting at that parameter. Args: c1, c2 : 4-point tuple cubics seeds : iterable of (t, u) starting pairs. Default brackets the c1-end / c2-start corner, which is the corner-rebuild case. limit : reject parameters outside [-limit, 1 + limit] - keeps far-field roots of the cubic continuation out of results tolerance : residual |C1(t) - C2(u)| accepted as a root Returns: list of (t1, t2, (x, y)), de-duplicated, sorted by t1. Empty when the extensions never meet (parallel tangents or divergent iteration).
title: typerig.core.algo.intersect.curve_curve_intersections_extended
